children: on Tuesday announced that its GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist enicepatide (CT-388) caused roughly 16% weight loss over a period of approximately 12 months in a mid-stage trial for obese or overweight adults with type 2 diabetes.

The once-weekly injectable, which the Swiss drugmaker added from its $2.7B acquisition of Carmot Therapeutics in 2024, reached both primary endpoints in its Phase 2 CT-388-104 study, the company said.
According to topline data, CT-388-104 hit the dual primary endpoints, generating dose-dependent and clinically meaningful declines in blood glucose and body weight over a period of 48 weeks.

Patients receiving the highest 24 mg dose of CT-388 had a 2.65% reduction in HbA1c, a diabetes biomarker, while their average weight loss reached 15.5% without a noticeable plateauing of weight reduction.

said that the safety and tolerability of enicapatide were in line with other drugs in its incretin-based therapeutic class. However, 2% of trial subjects dropped out due to adverse events compared with none in the placebo arm.
